doc.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998

title: What counts as jazz; Kenny G
summary: She doesn't spend energy on who is called jazz.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well you’ve certainly been doing it. I know Down Beat has recognized you as a top instrumentalist on your instrument. Are you bothered at all by — let me start again with that — contemporary jazz, where they put Kenny G and a few other folks in the jazz bins, do you think that that term is healthy for the music?

I don’t know. Words don’t mean that much to me. I don’t think about it that much with that kind of perspective who they call jazz or not jazz. Is it important or isn’t it? It’s a hard question. I have to kind of plead — from the view of most performing musicians, our concentration is really on doing the thing. I don’t sit around thinking about that, you know to be honest.
No not just that but you know that’s not, yeah, it’s just not where my attention is, it’s not where I put my energy into thinking about.
Yeah, it’s true you know. You know Kenny G can do whatever he wants you know.
